group: counter eating a block, rebuilt about 4/3 larger
title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1RC1LD_0LA1RA_1LE0RC_---1LF_0LA0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1RC1LD_0LA1RA_1LE0RC_---1LF_0LA0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps a long block of a = 111110 once per increment of a small counter, which eats a block of c = 1110; when the c's run out the tape is rebuilt and the next c-block is about 4/3 as long. The sweeps and the counter's twelve-trip cycle are proved in Lean for all lengths. A closed-set search with all remainders allowed found no halting class in 1.4 million rounds, but did not close: the short tail left of each rebuild takes more than 238,000 forms.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 41,526 cells have been visited and 28,752 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.53). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: The sweeps over the long block
claims.text: Going right in state A each pair aa becomes 101110101101 (32 steps per pair); going left in state E it is written back. Proved for all lengths and any tapes around.

claims.title: Rounds, observed
claims.text: At the left end the tape is F> 0 a^N [counter] c^M ...; each round trip increments the counter, which consumes c's. The values of M when a round starts: 24, 36, 50, 72, 116, 170, 248, 342, 454, 613, 814, 1100, 1466, 1967, 2628, a ratio of about 4/3. Seen in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Where it would halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is E reading 0, and E is entered only from D reading 0, so the machine halts exactly when the head in state D reads 0 with a 0 to its left (from the transition table).

claims.title: The counter's cycle
claims.text: With a = 111110, c = 1<sup>11</sup>0 and the engine word X = 7 a a 7 a a 7 a a 7 a 1<sup>4</sup> (7 = 1<sup>7</sup>0): twelve round trips take 0<sup>∞</sup> F> 0 a<sup>N</sup> X c<sup>M+6</sup> R to 0<sup>∞</sup> F> 0 a<sup>N+16</sup> X c<sup>M</sup> R, for every N ≥ 2, every M and any tape R. The counter eats 6 c and makes 16 a.

claims.title: No remainder class halts (sampled)
claims.text: Every round starts as 0<sup>∞</sup> F> 0 PRE c<sup>M</sup> TAIL with a fixed PRE. The next M is (4M + k)/3 and the next tail depends on the tail and on M mod 6. Following every residue from every tail found, the C simulator ran about 1.4 million rounds from more than 238,000 tails without a halt. The set of tails did not close: 50,000 were still unexplored.

claims.title: Why the closed-set method does not finish
claims.text: The tails are not a few families with a free count, and a pushdown closure of the tape language (one half summarised, the other an exact stack) either reports halts the real run does not have or runs out of memory. A proof needs a regular description of all tails that is closed under the round map.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rules for the counter and for the rebuild when the c's run out, and so a map M → M', are not found yet (see "For later" in the README).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LD_0LC1RC_1RA1RD_1LE0RB_---1LF_0LC0LA up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a long block on the left, sweeps it once for every tick of a small counter, and lets the counter eat a second block; when that block is gone the tape is rebuilt about a third larger. The sweeps are proved; the counter and the rebuild are still being decoded.

facts.text: Proved in Lean for all block lengths.
Observed growth of the eaten block from round to round.
Counter and rebuild rules not yet found.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: A long block, a counter, and its food
html: With a = 111110 and c = 1110, when the head is at the left end the tape reads

for example F>0 a^974 1111 aa 11 aaa 11 aaa 11 aaa 11 aa 1111 c^86 ... at step 27,213,697. Each round trip of the head (about 25N steps) rewrites the long block on the way right, pair by pair, and writes it back on the way left; this is proved in Lean. It also increments the counter in the middle, which eats c's as it carries, and adds a cell at the left end, so the left side grows like the square root of time.

sections.heading: Rounds about 4/3 larger
html: When the c's run out the blocks are rebuilt and a new round starts. The lengths M of the c-block at the starts of the rounds:
a ratio of about 4/3 per round. The number of rounds grows like the logarithm of time, the right side of the tape with it.

sections.heading: Open
html: The machine halts exactly when the head in state D reads 0 with a 0 to its left. The sweeps never do that. Whether a rebuild can depends on the exact rebuild rule, which looks like a Collatz-like map (multiply by about 4/3, with the remainder deciding the details); it has not been written down yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.53). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 41,526 cells (29,737 left of the start, 954 right), with a density of 1s of 0.692.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A long block a^N, a counter and a block c^M that the counter consumes; rebuilt with M about 4/3 larger. Sweeps and the counter's 12-trip cycle proved in Lean. Closed-set search: no halting class in 1.4 million rounds, but more than 238,000 tails, not closed.
